text:
Sam: FYI support ticket 87421 — customer reports intermittent ENOTFOUND when hitting internal service svc.payments.internal.redwood.example from their Dedicated VPC. Started after a change last night.

Sam: Error from their app: "getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND svc.payments.internal.redwood.example". They can curl other public endpoints fine.

Jordan: Can you paste a simple repro (curl + dig) they ran? Also which account/VPC is the hosted zone in?

Sam: They ran this: ```dig svc.payments.internal.redwood.example +short @169.254.169.253``` -> no output.

Sam: App pod nslookup shows NXDOMAIN. They say we recently associated private hosted zone "internal.redwood.example" to a shared-services VPC in account B.

Maria: Okay two quick possibilities: 1) overlapping private hosted zone with same name in a different account/VPC association order, 2) resolver rules pointing to a custom DNS (VPC Resolver) that isn't reachable from app VPC.

Ash: Also check VPC's DHCP option set / resolver endpoint — if they have a firewall/egress allowlist blocking outbound UDP/TCP 53 to the resolver IPs that will cause ENOTFOUND for internal names.

Sam: Customer says security group egress is wide open, but company-wide egress proxy could be intercepting port 53.

Jordan: Can they run these from a failing host: ```
# from app host/pod
cat /etc/resolv.conf
systemd-resolve --status || true
dig +trace svc.payments.internal.redwood.example
dig @172.31.0.2 svc.payments.internal.redwood.example +short
curl -v --resolve svc.payments.internal.redwood.example:443:10.0.12.34 https://svc.payments.internal.redwood.example/health
```

Sam: They ran resolv.conf: nameserver 172.31.0.2
Sam: dig @172.31.0.2 svc.payments.internal.redwood.example +short -> NXDOMAIN

Maria: Run aws CLI in account that owns the hosted zone and list VPC associations. If the hosted zone was associated to the wrong VPC (or removed) you'll see it. Example: ```aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z12345``` and ```aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id Z12345```

Ash: Also check cross-account association authorization if the hosted zone is in a different account. Route53 requires explicit authorization to associate a hosted zone from account A into VPC in account B. If someone accidentally associated a different hosted zone with the same name from a staging account, queries will hit the wrong zone and return NXDOMAIN for records missing there.

Sam: We pulled the hosted zones. There are two private hosted zones named internal.redwood.example: Z-A (account infra) and Z-B (account staging). Z-B was accidentally associated to the customer's VPC earlier today. Z-B does not contain svc.payments entries.

Jordan: That matches — duplicate private zones with same name will cause the resolver to use the hosted zone associated to that VPC (order is effectively which association exists). If Z-B is associated to the customer's VPC, queries resolve against Z-B and return NXDOMAIN.

Sam: How should we fix it? Customer asked for a rollback.

Maria: Remove the incorrect VPC association from Z-B or associate Z-A (the correct zone) with the VPC, but be careful: cross-account association needs the owner to authorize. Steps: 1) In account B (staging) run `aws route53 disassociate-vpc-from-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z-B --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0abc` 2) In account infra (Z-A) ensure association is present or run `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` (with authorization).

Ash: If you can't change associations immediately, a temporary workaround is to update the pod/node DNS to query a specific authoritative resolver (e.g., 169.254.169.253 or the infra VPC resolver endpoint) but that's fragile. Better to fix hosted zone associations.

Sam: Customer wants us to do the disassociate. They gave authorization for our infra team to act in their account.

infra-bot: Route53 change Z-B disassociation initiated by infra-user at 2026-03-17T21:02:00Z — change id /Z2ABCDEF/ABCDEFG

Sam: After disassociation, customer re-ran dig @172.31.0.2 svc.payments.internal.redwood.example +short -> 10.0.12.34

Sam: curl --resolve succeeded and TLS looked fine. Certificate CN matched internal wildcard.

Jordan: Add a postmortem note: accidental cross-account association of staging hosted zone to production VPC. Action items: 1) add guardrail to prevent private hosted zone names in staging that match prod (naming policy), 2) require approval for cross-account association changes, 3) add monitoring for unexpected VPC associations.

Maria: Also add an alert rule: any NXDOMAIN spike for internal.redwood.example in telemetry should page infra.

Sam: Closing ticket, customer confirmed svc healthy. Thanks team :thumbsup:
